title: US-Canada Trade Talks Collapse, 50% Tariffs on $20B of Canadian Goods Take Effect
detail: Trade negotiations between the US and Canada fell apart late Friday night, August 21, 2026, just before a midnight deadline — a dramatic reversal from Trump's August 18 announcement that the two sides 'have a DEAL!' Prime Minister Mark Carney said the US 'asked too much, and offered too little' with last-minute changes to the terms, including efforts to restrict Canada's ability to strike other trade deals and to weaken French-language and cultural protections tied to Canada's Online Streaming Act; Washington had also refused to extend tariff relief to medium and heavy trucks. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said Canada 'declined to finalize the trade deal under the terms agreed earlier this week,' while Trump posted that Canada 'wants the benefits of being a State, without being one.' With talks suspended, 50% Section 338 tariffs on roughly $20 billion of Canadian dairy, alcohol, furniture, and other goods took effect; Carney vowed 'dollar-for-dollar' retaliatory tariffs on US steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp, paper, and electronics starting September 8.

title: Trump Rallies in Myrtle Beach for Darline Graham Ahead of SC Senate Runoff
detail: President Trump held an 80-minute rally at the Myrtle Beach Convention Center on Friday, August 21, 2026, campaigning for Sen. Darline Graham ahead of her August 25 Republican runoff against Rep. Ralph Norman for the Senate seat vacated by her late brother, Lindsey Graham. Trump invoked Lindsey Graham's memory — 'For Lindsey, I want it to happen' — named Darline nearly 50 times, and defended her admission during a debate that she lacked national-security expertise, calling it 'being honest.' He also pledged federal funding for an Interstate 73 extension north from Myrtle Beach. Several thousand supporters attended in extreme heat; first responders treated multiple cases of heat exhaustion.

media.caption: Trump rallies for Sen. Darline Graham at the Myrtle Beach Convention Center ahead of her Senate runoff
